items.title: Define the canonical typed agent registry and compatibility aliases
items.context: Model role class, allowed phases, identifier cardinality/kinds, prompt builder, permitted mutations, commit guidance, reviewer lane, and evidence ownership. Legacy verification/test aliases must be deliberate entries, never prefix fallbacks.

happy.desc: Enumerate every canonical agent type in the typed registry and assert each entry declares role class, allowed phases, identifier cardinality/kinds, prompt class/builder, permitted mutation classes, commit guidance, reviewer lane, and evidence ownership with no missing required field -> the registry validates and yields one complete policy per type; WHY: establishes one mechanically inspectable dispatch truth source.

Resolve every supported legacy verification/test alias through the registry -> each alias maps to exactly one canonical type and inherits the canonical policy without prefix inference; WHY: preserves deliberate compatibility while preventing divergent alias behavior.

edge.desc: Enumerate canonical names and aliases together, including aliases that resemble reviewer or implementer prefixes -> names are unique, aliases do not collide with canonical entries or each other, and resolution is deterministic; WHY: catches ambiguous compatibility mappings at the registry boundary.

Inspect phase and identifier constraints for story-level and item-level roles -> empty/one/multiple identifier cases are represented explicitly by cardinality and allowed identifier kinds rather than implicit defaults; WHY: makes later schema and hint generation share exact boundary semantics.

adversarial.desc: Resolve an unknown, empty, case-mutated, or prefix-only agent type -> resolution fails closed before returning any role, prompt, mutation permission, commit guidance, or evidence policy; WHY: proves removed prefix fallback cannot silently classify unknown agents.

Attempt to construct a registry entry that omits a required policy field or grants an undeclared mutation class -> registry validation rejects it; WHY: prevents partial entries from recreating scattered defaults.

items.userSees: The dispatch registry diagnostic lists each supported canonical role and legacy alias with its lifecycle phases, target cardinality, prompt class, and authority class; duplicate or incomplete entries fail the diagnostic.

items.title: Route dispatch schemas, handlers, prompts, and hints through the registry
items.context: Unknown agent types must fail before prompt generation; story-level hints must be accepted by the same cardinality contract; reviewer and verification-intent roles must never receive implementer commit/status guidance.

happy.desc: For every canonical type and compatibility alias, exercise dispatch through schema validation and handler prompt construction in each allowed phase with valid story/item identifiers -> dispatch succeeds and the emitted prompt class, reviewer lane, evidence ownership, mutation permissions, and commit guidance equal the resolved registry policy; WHY: proves schema, handler, prompt, and permissions consume one registry decision.

Generate story-level and item-level dispatch hints for roles allowed at those cardinalities, then execute the exact example payloads through the CLI schema -> every displayed hint is schema-valid and accepted by the handler under the same cardinality contract; WHY: eliminates documentation/CLI disagreement.

edge.desc: Dispatch each role at every phase boundary and with zero, one, and extra identifiers -> only registry-declared phase/cardinality/kind combinations pass, and all rejected combinations return a specific contract error without prompt generation; WHY: verifies boundary parity among schema and handler.

Dispatch verification-intent, legacy test-intent/test-case-reviewer aliases, and all reviewer roles -> prompts contain their declared review/verification duties but contain no implementer commit author, implementation instruction, or checklist status=done guidance; WHY: prevents non-implementers receiving mutation-producing prompts.

adversarial.desc: Submit unknown or prefix-lookalike agent types directly to both command schema and handler entry points -> both fail closed before prompt construction and produce no mutation/evidence side effect; WHY: prevents schema bypass from reviving permissive routing.

Ask a reviewer or verification-intent role to invoke an implementer-only mutation class, and ask an implementer to invoke reviewer-pass/finding ownership mutations -> authorization rejects every denied command class and leaves story/checklist state unchanged; WHY: proves registry permissions are enforced, not merely described in prompts.

items.userSees: lattice dispatch returns role-safe prompts for valid story/item/finding/cluster calls; verification roles see no implementer commit or status:done steps, and unknown or wrong-cardinality calls exit nonzero with an actionable accepted-shape message.

items.title: Prove every type, alias, phase, cardinality, prompt class, and denied command class
items.context: Add table-driven positive and negative coverage, validate schema-valid example payloads, and update process-fact registry/contract verification whenever gate-consumed reviewer semantics change.

happy.desc: Run a table-driven matrix containing every canonical type and alias crossed with every lifecycle phase, supported identifier kind/cardinality, and expected prompt class -> each row matches registry policy and every registry entry/alias appears at least once; WHY: supplies exhaustive positive coverage and detects untested additions.

Run process-fact contract verification after registering any changed gate-consumed reviewer lane, evidence ownership, or dispatch semantics -> registry and verification script agree and the contract check passes; WHY: preserves the required prompt-plus-mechanical-gate dual contract.

edge.desc: Derive test rows from the registry and compare coverage sets -> cardinality is exact for canonical types, aliases, phases, identifier forms, prompt classes, permitted mutations, and denied mutations, with no duplicate or orphan rows; WHY: makes completeness mechanically measurable rather than asserted.

Parse every CLI hint/example produced for story-level and item-level dispatch and validate it against the public command schema -> examples are valid JSON, use accepted field names, and satisfy the same phase/cardinality rules; WHY: prevents syntactically plausible but unusable guidance.

adversarial.desc: For every matrix row, mutate one dimension at a time to an unknown type, disallowed alias spelling, wrong phase, wrong identifier kind/count, mismatched prompt class, or denied mutation class -> each negative case fails closed with no prompt or state mutation; WHY: proves all registry axes are enforcement boundaries.

Add a synthetic registry type or alias without adding corresponding matrix coverage and process-fact registration where required -> completeness/contract tests fail with the missing type or semantic explicitly identified; WHY: stops future registry growth from bypassing coverage and audit obligations.

items.userSees: The table-driven dispatch smoke reports every registry entry, alias, allowed and denied phase/cardinality/prompt/command case PASS, and process-fact verification confirms the same authority contract.
